messages:
maria: Heads-up — I see a ~3.5% Rouge-L drop on AWQ-INT8 in last night's prefetched continuous-batching run when prefix-cache is enabled for long-context summarization. Repro notes below.

maria: Experiment summary: model=voyager-13b-awq-int8, workload=redwood_long_summ_v2 (avg prompt ~320 tokens), serving=continuous-batcher, prefetch=true, prefix_cache_ttl=300s. Observed divergence vs fp8 baseline.

maria: Config (snippet):
```
model: voyager-13b-awq-int8
batcher:
  mode: continuous
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  pack_threshold_ms: 12
prefetch: true
prefix_cache:
  enabled: true
  ttl_s: 300
```

raj: Can you paste the eval harness output and which eval slice?

maria: Eval set = redwood_long_summ_v2 (300 examples). Key metrics: Rouge-L: fp8=41.8, awq-int8=38.3 (-3.5); perplexity: +18%. Main failure: entity drops & hallucinated dates on >256 token prompts. Snippet of results:
```
{"rouge_l": 38.3, "rouge_l_fp8": 41.8, "delta": -3.5}
```

ci-bot: Daily-eval (1861199900) finished — artifacts at https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/1861199900/redwood_long_summ_v2 (public link restricted)

sam: Did you isolate batching? try batching.mode=single or max_batch_tokens=1 to see if it's purely quantization or interaction with batching.

maria: Good call — ran single-request mode. AWQ-INT8 vs FP8 delta goes down to ~0.3% (within noise). So batching interaction + prefix cache looks like the culprit, not pure model quantization.

olga: My suspicion: kv-cache aliasing or reuse. Quantized kernels can change numerical traces and continuous batching with prefetch may reuse prefix cache entries that are only bitwise-equal for fp8 path. Rounding differences -> different cached states -> cascading divergence.

kevin: Two quick mitigations: 1) include quantization-profile/hash in prefix-cache key, 2) disable prefix-cache for first N tokens or for certain qprofiles. Either should avoid stale-hit mismatch.

raj: Do you have diffs by prompt length?

maria: Short/medium/long breakdown:
- short (<=64 tokens): delta = -0.1
- mid (65-256): delta = -1.2
- long (>256): delta = -3.5
So effect strongly correlated with prompt length + prefetch.

sam: Also check pack ordering. Continuous batching sometimes mixes short lead and long follow which can cause cache pointer reuse. Try deterministic packing or segregate by length.

maria: Repro script / command we used: 
```bash
./run_eval.sh --model voyager-13b-awq-int8 --eval redwood_long_summ_v2 --batcher continuous --prefetch yes --prefix-cache-ttl 300
```

olga: I pushed a tiny patch to add qprofile to cache key in feature/kv-qkey branch. It tags keys like: "prefix:<hash_of_prompt>:q=awq-int8". Kicking off full eval matrix now.

ci-bot: CI: build passed for branch feature/kv-qkey, running eval matrix (awq-int8,gptq-int8,fp8) x {prefetch on/off} x {batcher=continuous/single}. Will post results.

maria: If that fixes it, deployment plan: keep awq-int8 for short prompts but route long prompts to fp8 by default until we validate. Safer to avoid user-visible regressions.

kevin: Proposed rollout: canary 10% on dedicated with monitoring hooks for Rouge/regression + latency. Alert if rouge_delta > 1.0 over canary samples for 15m -> auto-fallback to fp8. Also include cost watch: fp8 ~+10-15% cost.

raj: Agreed. Also make sure eval set covers variety of entity-heavy long prompts (we saw entity drops). Add synthetic entity stress tests.

sam: Note: disabling prefix-cache will increase token-gen cost (more KV work) and may push p99 by ~30-40ms in our perf sims. We need tradeoffs in deployment config.

maria: Plan of record: 1) Run full matrix with qkey patch, batching modes, prefix_cache toggles, track rouge/ppl/latency & cost. 2) If qkey patch resolves divergence, add qprofile into prefix-cache key globally behind a flag. 3) If not resolved, route long prompts to fp8 with canary+auto-fallback. I'll commit the CSVs under experiments/kv-cache-qprofile and share artifacts.

olga: Assigning follow-ups: @maria run matrix and upload, @kevin draft rollout policy and canary config, @raj expand eval slices.

kevin: :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — I'll post interim numbers once full matrix finishes (CI ETA ~2h).
